analysis:
The PR threads an optional per-request stop-string scope (CBv2StopStringScope) through EngineV2Bridge: submitTokenized (+Submission.swift lines 61, 80, 129-131, 254-259, 948) -> cbv2Request.stopStringScope -> runPump/pump (+Events.swift lines 15, 32, 64, 150-151) -> matchedStopSequence (+StopSequence.swift lines 5-36). It is a correctness/metadata change, which affects which stop string is reported as matched when a scope such as the Harmony analysis channel is in play. I found no security-relevant regression.

Examined points:
- No change to cryptography, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache scoping or salt derivation (T-041 salt/HMAC paths are untouched), or disk I/O.
- Resource release paths in pump (KV reservation, prefix receipts, retirement wait, usageSignal finalization) are unchanged; the diff only adds a parameter.
- Stop sequences and scope come from the request translation, not from new untrusted wire fields visible in this diff. The consumer can already supply stop strings, and they are not used in telemetry. Telemetry stays content-free.
- The scoped matcher re-ingests the decoded text through StopHoldback once for the full candidate list and then once per candidate. This is O(candidates x text length) on the pump's actor at terminal time. The number of candidates is presumably bounded by request validation, which is outside the supplied evidence. A very large candidate list could cause a minor availability cost, but I have no evidence of an unbounded list, so this is recorded as an open question rather than a finding.
- In the native block engine, requests carry no scope (stopStringScope is nil when ownedEngine is CBv2NativeBlockEngine), so matching falls back to the legacy whole-output scan. This is consistent with the stated engine behavior.
- Open integration items: the StopHoldback and CBv2StopStringScope implementations, whether EngineLoopV2 honors request.stopStringScope, and the callers that pass stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope) were not supplied. The Submission.swift patch excerpt is truncated, but the head change at line 948 is visible. A mismatch between the reported and the actual stop sequence would affect only response metadata and not confidentiality.
